haiku-low.q1: They do not differ. Both get 401 with the identical 'Invalid email or password' page. Unknown emails run bcrypt against a dummy hash to take similar time.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with a try-again-later login page. The password is not checked and no failure is recorded.
haiku-low.q3: It is deleted in the same transaction that creates the new session, after the password is verified. The old ID is dead from that moment.
haiku-low.q4: Only a random session ID, which is a base64url value (sid). Cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It also has Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours from login, the absolute limit ends it, even with constant use. Each request restarts only the 30-minute idle clock.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes that session row by hash if present, clears the sid cookie, and redirects with 303 to /login.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row by hash and waits for confirmation, then replies 303 to /login with the cookie cleared. A missing session affects 0 rows and gets the same response.
haiku-low.q8: In Postgres tables (sessions, and others) shared by both instances. Any instance looks up the hashed cookie ID there, so no sticky sessions are needed.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failure with email and failed_at. The server counts rows where failed_at is later than now() minus 10 minutes, using Postgres now().
haiku-low.q10: It compares the hashed cookie to a sessions row with last_seen_at under 30 minutes old and created_at under 12 hours old. On success it writes last_seen_at = now().
haiku-low.q11: A generic 503 page reading 'Something went wrong. Please try again in a moment.' with no Set-Cookie, so no new session cookie is set.
haiku-low.q12: A sweep every 5 minutes on each instance deletes expired sessions, failures older than 10 minutes, and unlocked throttle rows with no recent failures.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get a 401 login page with the identical body "Invalid email or password". The server runs bcrypt against a dummy hash for unknown emails so timing is similar.
sonnet.q2: The 5th failure already set locked_until = now() + 15 min. The next attempt gets a 429 login page ("try again later"). The password is not checked and no failure is recorded. This holds while locked_until is in the future, i.e. for 15 minutes.
sonnet.q3: If the login succeeds, the old session row is deleted in the same transaction that inserts a brand-new session with a fresh random ID. The old ID is dead from commit onward. The new cookie is set only after commit. If the login fails, the old cookie is unchanged.
sonnet.q4: Only a random session ID (32 CSPRNG bytes, base64url). Page scripts cannot read it because the cookie is HttpOnly. It is also Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/.
sonnet.q5: At the absolute limit, 12 hours after login. Activity keeps restarting the 30-minute idle clock, but the absolute limit (created_at + 12 h) is not extended.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns zero rows. The server runs DELETE of the session by hash (harmless if absent), clears the sid cookie (Max-Age=0), and answers 303 redirect to /login.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, the server runs DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id_hash and waits for it to finish. If the session is already gone, it deletes 0 rows, which is fine. It still replies 303 to /login with the cookie cleared, the same as when a session existed. If the delete can't be confirmed, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres `sessions` table, which both instances share. Any instance hashes the cookie's ID with SHA-256 and looks up the row by id_hash in Postgres on every protected request. No sticky sessions or Redis are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres table login_failures (email, failed_at), with an index on (email, failed_at). The window is decided by counting the email's rows where failed_at > now() - 10 min. Postgres now() is the clock, not the app instance's clock.
sonnet.q10: It compares, against Postgres now(), that last_seen_at is within 30 minutes (last_seen_at > now() - 30 min) and that created_at is within 12 hours (created_at > now() - 12 h), matched by id_hash. It does this in one atomic UPDATE. On success it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 generic error page ("Something went wrong. Please try again in a moment.") with no Set-Cookie. The transaction is rolled back.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup sweep. An in-process timer on each instance runs every 5 minutes from boot and deletes sessions past the idle limit (30 min) or the absolute limit (12 h). Expired sessions presented by a returning browser are also deleted lazily.
